## Getting started

### Install

Grab the latest release with the install script:

```sh
curl -sSL https://get.sqlpipe.dev | sh
```

The script detects your platform, drops the `sqlpipe` binary in `/usr/local/bin`, and makes it executable. Verify with `sqlpipe --version`.

### Configure

sqlpipe reads its pipeline definition from a YAML file. Create `sqlpipe.yaml` in your project root:

```yaml
source:
  driver: postgres
  dsn: postgres://user:pass@localhost:5432/appdb

target:
  driver: mysql
  dsn: mysql://user:pass@localhost:3306/warehouse

tables:
  - name: orders
  - name: customers
```

Keep credentials out of version control: any `${VAR}` in the file is expanded from the environment at load time.

### First run

```sh
sqlpipe run --config sqlpipe.yaml
```

sqlpipe validates both connections, then streams each listed table from source to target, printing per-table row counts as it goes. A non-zero exit code means at least one table failed; re-running is safe, since transfers are idempotent.
